title: Supermoiré Chern mosaic in helical trilayer WSe2
comment: 30 pages, including 4 main figures and 10 supplemental figures
summary: Helically twisted multilayers offer access to moiré physics beyond the single-superlattice paradigm, yet their correlated and topological transport properties remain largely unexplored in semiconductor moiré materials. Here we report magnetotransport measurements of helical trilayer WSe2, in which two coupled moiré patterns relax into a supermoiré landscape composed of inequivalent local topological domains with distinct electronic structures and unequal spatial areas. By electrostatic tuning, we identify a trilayer-hybridized regime where interactions and real-space reconstruction combine to generate a plethora of magnetic and topological states absent in the twisted bilayers. At moiré filling factor $ν$ = -1, we observe a ferromagnetic insulating state that is robust against magnetic field and accompanied by a non-quantized anomalous Hall response ~-4 kOhms. This behaviour is consistent with a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking supermoiré Chern mosaic, in which the Hall response arises from the non-cancelling contributions of local domains with opposite Chern character arranged by the relaxed structure. Under strong magnetic fields, a symmetry-broken Chern insulating state (C = 1) emerges near $ν$ = -2/3, displaying a much larger positive Hall response together with strongly enhanced longitudinal resistance, suggestive of field-reconstructed topological minibands and domain-boundary scattering. These results establish relaxed supermoiré semiconductor trilayers as a platform for spatially organized magnetism and topology beyond the bilayer limit.

AI.tldr: The paper reports magnetotransport measurements on helical trilayer WSe2, revealing ferromagnetic insulating states and anomalous Hall effects arising from a supermoiré Chern mosaic—a landscape of inequivalent topological domains created by the relaxation of two coupled moiré patterns. These findings establish supermoiré semiconductor trilayers as a platform for spatially organized magnetism and topology beyond bilayer moiré systems.
AI.motivation: To explore correlated and topological transport properties in helically twisted semiconductor multilayers beyond the single-superlattice (bilayer) paradigm, where two coupled moiré patterns create a richer supermoiré landscape.
AI.method: Magnetotransport measurements on helical trilayer WSe2 with electrostatic tuning, probing moiré filling factors near ν = -1 and ν = -2/3 under varying magnetic fields.
AI.result: At ν = -1: a ferromagnetic insulating state with robust, non-quantized anomalous Hall response (~-4 kΩ). At ν = -2/3 under strong fields: a symmetry-broken Chern insulating state (C = 1) with large positive Hall response and enhanced longitudinal resistance, suggesting field-reconstructed minibands and domain-boundary scattering.
AI.conclusion: Relaxed supermoiré semiconductor trilayers provide a platform for spatially organized magnetism and topology, featuring a Chern mosaic of local topological domains with opposite Chern character that generate net Hall responses absent in twisted bilayers.

title: Geometry still matters in quasi-one-dimensional single-file transport
summary: Single-file transport means no overtaking: particles move in a narrow channel while preserving their longitudinal order. This simple constraint has profound dynamical consequences, most notably tracer subdiffusion, and has made single-file transport a paradigmatic form of confined many-body motion, observed from molecular transport in zeolites to single-file diffusion of colloids in narrow channels. The standard view is that, once overtaking is suppressed, collective transport reduces to that of a strictly one-dimensional file. Here we show that this reduction fails in experimentally relevant finite-width channels: even when exchange is forbidden, the transverse equilibrium structure controls the transport laws and can qualitatively reshape them. Starting from the Brownian dynamics in the full confined geometry, we derive an exact large-scale one-dimensional fluctuating hydrodynamics for the longitudinal density, whose coefficients are fixed by the confined equilibrium equation of state. In the minimal hard-core setting, this yields a collective diffusivity that can become non-monotonic in density. This geometric anomaly propagates to exact large-scale predictions for integrated-current fluctuations, tracer displacement fluctuations and the associated density profiles. The effect is robust to the interaction potential, channel geometry, initial preparation and microscopic dynamics. Quasi-one-dimensional single-file transport therefore defines a distinct regime in which forbidding overtaking does not erase geometry from collective transport.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that in quasi-one-dimensional channels with finite width, single-file transport (where overtaking is forbidden) does not simply reduce to strictly one-dimensional behavior. Instead, the transverse equilibrium structure qualitatively reshapes transport laws, producing non-monotonic collective diffusivity and modifying fluctuations, even when exchange is suppressed.
AI.motivation: To challenge the standard view that single-file transport in finite-width channels reduces to strictly one-dimensional file dynamics, and to demonstrate that transverse equilibrium structure qualitatively influences collective transport even when overtaking is forbidden.
AI.method: Starting from Brownian dynamics in the full confined geometry, the authors derive an exact large-scale one-dimensional fluctuating hydrodynamics for the longitudinal density, with coefficients determined by the confined equilibrium equation of state.
AI.result: In the minimal hard-core setting, the collective diffusivity becomes non-monotonic in density, a geometric anomaly that propagates to integrated-current fluctuations, tracer displacement fluctuations, and density profiles. The effect is robust to interaction potential, channel geometry, initial preparation, and microscopic dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Quasi-one-dimensional single-file transport defines a distinct regime where forbidding overtaking does not erase geometry from collective transport, contradicting the standard reduction to strictly one-dimensional behavior.

title: Magnetism and Topology from Circularly Polarized Phonon Floquet Engineering
summary: We theoretically show that circularly polarized phonons induce electronic magnetization and drive a topological phase transition via phonon Floquet engineering. Considering the electronic states modulated by circularly polarized phonons on a honeycomb lattice, we show that such lattice dynamics generates an effective next-nearest-neighbor electron hopping, leading to a Haldane-type mass term. Circularly polarized phonon breaks time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and opens a gap at valley points, undergoing phase transition from a trivial insulator to a Chern insulator. Moreover, the orbital and spin magnetizations emerge due to the breaking of TRS. Our results show that circularly polarized phonons serve as an effective magnetic field to engineer magnetism and topology, offering new opportunities for phonon Floquet approaches.

AI.tldr: Circularly polarized phonons can induce electronic magnetization and drive topological phase transitions (trivial insulator to Chern insulator) on a honeycomb lattice via phonon Floquet engineering, effectively acting as a magnetic field.
AI.motivation: To theoretically demonstrate that circularly polarized phonons can break time-reversal symmetry and induce both magnetism and topological phase transitions, serving as an effective magnetic field without real magnetic fields.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis using phonon Floquet engineering on a honeycomb lattice, showing that circularly polarized phonons generate effective next-nearest-neighbor electron hopping, which produces a Haldane-type mass term.
AI.result: Circularly polarized phonons break time-reversal symmetry, open a gap at valley points, drive a transition from trivial insulator to Chern insulator, and induce both orbital and spin magnetizations.
AI.conclusion: Circularly polarized phonons can serve as an effective magnetic field to engineer magnetism and topology, providing new opportunities for phonon Floquet approaches.

title: Majorana fermions at self-generated interfaces
summary: The Kitaev model describing a one-dimensional topological superconducting chain is known to support two Majorana fermions localized at the systems endpoints when the parameters are tuned to the topological phase. In this work, we investigate the possibility that Majorana fermions may also emerge away from the physical boundaries of the chain. To this purpose, we generalize the Kitaev model by incorporating a local coupling between the electronic density and a classical elastic (lattice) field. This electron-lattice interaction can induce phase separation between superconducting regions characterized by distinct topological invariants, thereby generating internal interfaces that host Majorana bound states. Under these conditions, a dilute gas of Majorana fermions can be realized in the bulk of the system.

AI.tldr: The Kitaev chain model is generalized by coupling electrons to a classical lattice field, inducing phase separation between topologically distinct superconducting regions. This creates internal interfaces that host Majorana bound states away from physical boundaries, enabling a dilute gas of Majorana fermions in the bulk.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether Majorana fermions can emerge away from the physical boundaries of a Kitaev chain, by introducing electron-lattice coupling to generate internal topological interfaces.
AI.method: Generalize the Kitaev model by incorporating a local coupling between electronic density and a classical elastic (lattice) field, which can induce phase separation between regions with distinct topological invariants.
AI.result: The electron-lattice interaction can induce phase separation between superconducting regions characterized by different topological invariants, generating internal interfaces that host Majorana bound states, realizing a dilute gas of Majorana fermions in the bulk.
AI.conclusion: Majorana fermions can emerge in the bulk of a generalized Kitaev chain through phase separation induced by electron-lattice coupling, not just at physical endpoints.

title: Influence of CeO$_2$MnO$_x$ heterostructure on Hydrogen Peroxide Electrogeneration on Carbon-Based Catalysts
summary: The sustainable electrogeneration of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e$^-$ ORR) represents a promising alternative to conventional production methods. In this study, CeO2 and CeO2MnOx nanoparticles were synthesized and supported on Vulcan XC-72 carbon at varying loadings (1, 3, and 5%), aiming to assess the lowest metal loading and high H2O2 electrosynthesis. Physicochemical characterizations confirmed the successful formation of CeO2 nanowires and the effectiveness of the MnOx surface modification. XRD, TEM, XPS, EPR, and contact angle analyses revealed that CeO2 loading increased surface hydrophilicity through the presence of oxygenated functional groups, thereby favoring electrochemical activity. On the other hand, all CeO2MnOx loadings were statistically equivalent to Vulcan XC-72 in terms of contact angle. Electrochemical evaluations using a rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE) demonstrated enhanced ORR activity and high H2O2 selectivity for the 1% CeO2MnOx/C and 3% CeO2/C catalysts, achieving up to 90% selectivity and elevated ring currents. The results suggest that low metal loading and surface modification via MnOx improve the balance between active site exposure, oxygen adsorption, and intermediate stabilization, thus favoring the selective 2e$^-$ pathway. These findings support the development of cost-effective, non-noble-metal catalysts for green H2O2 production via electrosynthesis.

AI.tldr: CeO₂ and CeO₂MnOx nanoparticles on carbon supports achieved up to 90% H₂O₂ selectivity via 2e⁻ ORR, with low metal loading (1–3%) enhancing activity through improved hydrophilicity and oxygen adsorption.
AI.motivation: To develop a cost-effective, non-noble-metal catalyst system for sustainable electrochemical H₂O₂ production, assessing the lowest possible metal loading while maintaining high selectivity and activity.
AI.method: CeO₂ and CeO₂MnOx nanoparticles were synthesized and supported on Vulcan XC-72 carbon at 1, 3, and 5% loadings; characterized by XRD, TEM, XPS, EPR, and contact angle; electrochemical performance evaluated via RRDE.
AI.result: 1% CeO₂MnOx/C and 3% CeO₂/C achieved up to 90% H₂O₂ selectivity with elevated ring currents; CeO₂ loading increased surface hydrophilicity; all CeO₂MnOx loadings showed contact angles equivalent to Vulcan XC-72.
AI.conclusion: Low metal loading with MnOx surface modification optimizes active site exposure, oxygen adsorption, and intermediate stabilization for selective 2e⁻ ORR, supporting development of affordable green H₂O₂ electrosynthesis catalysts.

title: Synthetic pre-training of graph-network models for predicting solid-state NMR parameters
summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a powerful probe of atomic structure, but accurate quantum-mechanical predictions of tensorial NMR parameters are computationally demanding. This creates a bottleneck both for direct quantum-mechanical studies and for collecting high-quality training data for machine-learning (ML) models. Here, we introduce a synthetic pre-training and fine-tuning protocol for graph-based ML models of solid-state NMR parameters. We first pre-train models on synthetic tensorial data, as obtained using an existing ML model, and subsequently fine-tune those models on new ground-truth data. We observe a pronounced improvement in data efficiency when pre-training and fine-tuning span the same compositional and configurational space, and we carry out initial experiments regarding chemical transferability. Our work outlines a route toward future data-efficient training workflows for tensorial ML models for solid-state NMR, combining inexpensive synthetic supervision with targeted first-principles refinement.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a synthetic pre-training and fine-tuning protocol for graph-based ML models of solid-state NMR parameters, improving data efficiency by combining inexpensive synthetic supervision with targeted first-principles refinement.
AI.motivation: Accurate quantum-mechanical predictions of tensorial NMR parameters are computationally demanding, creating a bottleneck for direct studies and for collecting high-quality training data for ML models.
AI.method: A synthetic pre-training and fine-tuning protocol for graph-based ML models: first pre-train on synthetic tensorial data from an existing ML model, then fine-tune on new ground-truth data.
AI.result: Pronounced improvement in data efficiency when pre-training and fine-tuning span the same compositional and configurational space; initial experiments on chemical transferability conducted.
AI.conclusion: The work outlines a route toward data-efficient training workflows for tensorial ML models for solid-state NMR, combining synthetic supervision with first-principles refinement.

title: Microscopic evidence for a Zhang-Rice triplet state in the van der Waals antiferromagnet, NiPS$_3$
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures; Accepted for publication in Physical Review Letters
summary: Quantum-entangled states underpin many emergent phenomena in quantum materials, yet their direct experimental identification remains a challenge. NiPS$_3$, a van der Waals antiferromagnet exhibiting a resolution-limited magnetic exciton in its ordered phase, has been proposed to host a many-body entangled Zhang-Rice triplet state. Here, using $^{33}$S nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) on $^{33}$S-enriched NiPS$_3$ single crystals, we provide microscopic evidence for this charge-transfer state. The $^{33}$S and $^{31}$P Knight shifts as a function of temperature reveal a unified spin-triplet configuration arising from strong hybridization between a self-doped hole in the S $3p$ orbitals and a hole in Ni $3d$ orbitals. Furthermore, the $^{33}$S nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate exhibits a power-law divergence as it approaches the Néel temperature $T_N=155$ K, indicating critical slowing down of collective charge fluctuations consistent with spin-nematic correlations. These results reveal a spin-charge-intertwined ground state and establish the microscopic foundation for the exceptional coherence of the magnetic exciton in NiPS$_3$.

AI.tldr: Using 33S NMR on enriched NiPS₃ single crystals, the study provides microscopic evidence for a many-body entangled Zhang-Rice triplet state, revealing a spin-charge-intertwined ground state with spin-nematic correlations that explains the coherence of the magnetic exciton.
AI.motivation: Quantum-entangled states are key to emergent phenomena in quantum materials, but direct experimental identification is challenging. NiPS₃ was proposed to host a many-body entangled Zhang-Rice triplet state, yet microscopic evidence was lacking.
AI.method: 33S NMR measurements on 33S-enriched NiPS₃ single crystals, analyzing 33S and 31P Knight shifts as a function of temperature, and measuring 33S nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate near the Néel temperature TN=155 K.
AI.result: Knight shift data reveal a unified spin-triplet configuration from strong hybridization between a self-doped hole in S 3p orbitals and a hole in Ni 3d orbitals. The 33S spin-lattice relaxation rate shows a power-law divergence approaching TN, indicating critical slowing down of collective charge fluctuations consistent with spin-nematic correlations.
AI.conclusion: The results reveal a spin-charge-intertwined ground state and establish the microscopic foundation for the exceptional coherence of the magnetic exciton in NiPS₃.

title: Robust AI-Driven Discovery of Electronic Metal Phosphide Semiconductors
comment: 46 pages, 5 main figures; Supporting Information included
summary: Metal phosphides have diverse bonding motifs and coordination environments, making them promising for optoelectronic and thermoelectric applications, but their chemical space remains underexplored. Here we report an AI-driven high-throughput discovery workflow that combines generative materials design, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and targeted density functional theory (DFT) calculations. ICSD-derived Wyckoff-site substitution and MatterGen-based conditional structure generation are used to expand the candidate space beyond existing phosphide databases. A domain-finetuned DPA3 machine-learning potential then enables efficient prescreening of thermodynamic and dynamical stability before DFT validation. This workflow identifies 3,574 previously unreported stable phosphide structures, including 196 semiconductors with HSE06 band gaps of 0-3.0 eV. By screening these new semiconductors together with experimentally known phosphide semiconductors, we identify 30 promising optoelectronic candidates and 26 promising thermoelectric candidates, including seven newly discovered optoelectronic materials and eight newly discovered thermoelectric materials. These results provide a candidate pool for experimental synthesis and show that combining generative AI with machine-learning interatomic potentials can accelerate the discovery of functional semiconductor materials.

AI.tldr: An AI-driven high-throughput workflow combining generative materials design, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and DFT calculations discovered 3,574 previously unreported stable phosphides, including 196 semiconductors, and identified 30 promising optoelectronic and 26 promising thermoelectric candidates.
AI.motivation: Metal phosphides have diverse bonding motifs and coordination environments suitable for optoelectronic and thermoelectric applications, but their chemical space remains underexplored due to lack of systematic discovery methods.
AI.method: The workflow integrates ICSD-derived Wyckoff-site substitution and MatterGen-based conditional structure generation to expand candidate space, a domain-finetuned DPA3 machine-learning potential for prescreening thermodynamic/dynamical stability, and DFT validation with HSE06 band gap calculations.
AI.result: 3,574 novel stable phosphides identified (196 semiconductors with 0-3.0 eV band gaps); 30 optoelectronic candidates (7 newly discovered) and 26 thermoelectric candidates (8 newly discovered) identified.
AI.conclusion: Combining generative AI with machine-learning interatomic potentials can accelerate the discovery of functional semiconductor materials, providing a candidate pool for experimental synthesis.

title: Extensible links in a broad class of single polymer chain models
summary: The physics of polymer chains is often probed using molecular stretching experiments and various idealized single-chain models. The majority of these models consist of a discrete sequence of links, which may be treated as rigid or extensible. Although such models are well established and many specific extensible variants have been proposed, no generally applicable theory has been presented. Moreover, most existing treatments are heuristic rather than systematically and rigorously derived. This critical gap is closed here through the development of a generally applicable asymptotic theory for including link extensibility in a broad class of discrete models for single-chain thermodynamics. The theory is verified analytically using the freely jointed chain and validated numerically using the freely rotating chain. The resulting approximation is first-order accurate in inverse link stiffness, with quadratically decreasing error, and recovers extensible behavior across all link stiffnesses from a single rigid-link reference calculation.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a general asymptotic theory for incorporating link extensibility into discrete single-chain thermodynamic models, verified analytically on freely jointed chains and numerically on freely rotating chains, achieving first-order accuracy in inverse link stiffness with quadratically decreasing error.
AI.motivation: Existing extensible chain models are heuristic and lack rigorous derivation; no generally applicable theory exists despite many specific variants being proposed.
AI.method: A general asymptotic theory for including link extensibility in discrete single-chain thermodynamic models, first-order accurate in inverse link stiffness.
AI.result: Verified analytically using the freely jointed chain and validated numerically using the freely rotating chain; error decreases quadratically, and extensible behavior across all link stiffnesses can be recovered from a single rigid-link reference calculation.
AI.conclusion: The theory closes a critical gap by providing a systematic, rigorous, and generally applicable framework for extensible link models in polymer chain thermodynamics.

title: Optical fingerprints across the strain-driven semi-Dirac transition in Kekulé-O graphene
summary: We show that the strain-driven semi-Dirac transition in Kekulé-O graphene gives rise to a sequence of anisotropic optical fingerprints associated with band structure reconstruction. Across the transition, optical spectral weight is continuously redistributed among the dominant interband transitions, leading to a pronounced enhancement of the optical anisotropy. Combining numerical four-band calculations with analytical low-energy results, we identify three low-energy fingerprints that emerge with increasing strain: gapped absorption peaks, semi-Dirac critical scaling, and a pronounced van Hove optical resonance. At the semi-Dirac critical point, where the Kekulé gap closes at the $Γ$ point, the low-energy optical conductivity is characterized by $σ_{xx}(Ω)\proptoΩ^{1/2}$ and $σ_{yy}(Ω)\proptoΩ^{-1/2}$. Beyond the transition, the semi-Dirac point splits into two anisotropic Dirac cones, accompanied by the emergence of saddle points near the $Γ$ point. The resulting saddle-point excitations produce a pronounced van Hove optical resonance at energies well below those of graphene, while the split Dirac cones give rise to an anisotropic constant optical conductivity. We further show that the low-energy optical fingerprints can be traced to the continuous evolution of a dominant optical transition channel driven by strain-induced band reconstruction. Moreover, the fingerprints remain identifiable in the presence of moderate disorder broadening and finite-temperature effects, indicating their potential observability under experimentally realistic conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the strain-driven semi-Dirac transition in Kekulé-O graphene, identifying three distinct low-energy optical fingerprints—gapped absorption peaks, semi-Dirac critical scaling with σ_xx ∝ Ω^{1/2} and σ_yy ∝ Ω^{-1/2}, and a van Hove optical resonance—that arise from band structure reconstruction. These fingerprints remain observable under moderate disorder and finite temperatures, suggesting experimental viability.
AI.motivation: To characterize the anisotropic optical signatures of the semi-Dirac transition in Kekulé-O graphene and determine whether these fingerprints are robust enough for experimental detection.
AI.method: Combined numerical four-band tight-binding calculations with analytical low-energy models to compute optical conductivity across the strain-driven transition, analyzing spectral weight redistribution and scaling behavior.
AI.result: Three low-energy optical fingerprints identified: (1) gapped absorption peaks, (2) semi-Dirac critical scaling (σ_xx∝Ω^{1/2}, σ_yy∝Ω^{-1/2}), and (3) a van Hove optical resonance from saddle points. Beyond the transition, split anisotropic Dirac cones produce constant anisotropic conductivity. All fingerprints persist under moderate disorder and finite temperature.
AI.conclusion: The strain-driven semi-Dirac transition in Kekulé-O graphene produces robust, experimentally observable anisotropic optical fingerprints that reflect the underlying band structure reconstruction.

title: On pseudogap phase as precursor to a superconducting dome in high-Tc cuprates: Non-analytic T* as a function of doping
summary: We generalize the condition under which a quantum material exhibiting a pseudogap phase is a precursor to a superconducting (SC) dome. The result reveals the non-analytic T* as a function of doping. A well-known example is the high-Tc cuprates. Essentially, the SC dome is generated under two conditions: (1) that the pseudogap T* is a decreasing function of doping, due to the decrease in size of extended pairing of doped holes with doping, and most importantly, (2) that the rate of configurational-ordering parameter is an increasing function of doping as a result of the decrease in extended length of the disordered pairs. These two conditions are provided by the new entanglement and confinement pairing mechanism of high-Tc cuprates. This is a theory that has recently been discussed in the literature by Buot et al. It hinges on a novel strong entanglement and confinement hole pairing (ECHP) mechanism that unravels the microscopic features of the entire phase diagram of both electron and hole-doped high-Tc cuprates.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes the conditions under which a pseudogap phase precedes a superconducting dome, identifying two key conditions: decreasing pseudogap T* with doping and increasing configurational-ordering parameter rate with doping. These are explained via the entanglement and confinement pairing mechanism (ECHP) for high-Tc cuprates.
AI.motivation: To generalize the condition linking pseudogap phases to superconducting domes in quantum materials, particularly to explain the non-analytic T* behavior as a function of doping in high-Tc cuprates.
AI.method: The paper derives two necessary conditions: (1) pseudogap T* decreases with doping due to reduced extended pairing of doped holes, and (2) the configurational-ordering parameter rate increases with doping due to shortened disordered pair lengths. These are grounded in the entanglement and confinement hole pairing (ECHP) mechanism.
AI.result: The SC dome emerges when both conditions are simultaneously satisfied: decreasing T*(doping) and increasing configurational-ordering rate. The ECHP mechanism provides the microscopic foundation for this behavior.
AI.conclusion: The ECHP mechanism successfully unravels the microscopic features of the entire phase diagram for both electron and hole-doped high-Tc cuprates, establishing pseudogap as a precursor to superconductivity under specific doping-dependent conditions.

title: SANS and magnetometry study of the magnetic phase diagram of the B20 helimagnet FeRhSi
summary: This manuscript reports the first direct neutron-scattering evidence for long-period helimagnetism in the newly identified 4d-substituted B20 compound Fe0.5Rh0.5Si. By combining SANS with low-field magnetometry, we establish the magnetic modulation, construct a field-temperature phase diagram, and identify a candidate A-phase region supported by an independent structural signature. The work is important beyond this single compound because it expands the family of chiral B20 helimagnets into Rh-substituted materials, where spin-orbit coupling, disorder, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions can be tuned. It will interest researchers in chiral magnetism, topological spin textures, magnetic neutron scattering, and quantum materials, and provides a foundation for future studies of emergent magnetic phases and topology-driven phenomena in chemically tuned chiral magnets.

AI.tldr: First direct neutron-scattering evidence for long-period helimagnetism in Fe0.5Rh0.5Si, a 4d-substituted B20 compound, with field-temperature phase diagram and candidate A-phase region identified via SANS and magnetometry.
AI.motivation: Expand the family of chiral B20 helimagnets into Rh-substituted materials, enabling tunable spin-orbit coupling, disorder, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions.
AI.method: Combined small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) with low-field magnetometry to establish magnetic modulation and construct a field-temperature phase diagram.
AI.result: Identified long-period helimagnetism and a candidate A-phase region supported by an independent structural signature in Fe0.5Rh0.5Si.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a foundation for studying emergent magnetic phases and topology-driven phenomena in chemically tuned chiral magnets.

title: Neural electron backscatter diffraction
summary: In a polycrystalline microstructure, orientation and dislocation content vary smoothly within grains, and the grain boundaries between them are continuous curves. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) records this continuum on a discrete grid with every subsequent analysis (from indexing to advanced pattern processing) confined to that grid. We introduce neural EBSD, which treats an EBSD scan as a continuous, differentiable four-dimensional field of Kikuchi diffraction intensity (in specimen--detector domain) and then represents it with a coordinate-based neural network. We develop and compare two formulations: a joint formulation that maps all four coordinates to intensity, and a factorized formulation that combines continuous specimen-domain coefficient fields with learned detector-domain basis patterns. Tested on recrystallized and additively manufactured Inconel 718, the factorized formulation shows better accuracy in reconstructing Kikuchi patterns that have map-averaged errors below 1% of the maximum intensity. Beyond reconstruction, it provides full-pattern super-resolution in the specimen frame, continuous querying along arbitrary off-grid paths, as well as spatially continuous boundary and heterogeneity localization from analytical spatial derivatives. Storing the network weights and learned bases in place of the raw patterns in a large dataset offers a 700-fold compression while preserving on-demand access to the full patterns for downstream analyses.

AI.tldr: Neural EBSD treats EBSD scans as continuous 4D Kikuchi intensity fields using coordinate-based neural networks, achieving high reconstruction accuracy (<1% error), super-resolution, continuous spatial querying, and 700× compression on Inconel 718.
AI.motivation: Traditional EBSD analysis is constrained to discrete grid data, losing the continuous nature of microstructural features (orientation, dislocation content, grain boundaries). This paper aims to overcome the discretization limitations of conventional EBSD processing.
AI.method: Two neural network formulations are developed: (1) a joint formulation mapping all four coordinates (specimen x,y + detector coordinates) directly to intensity; (2) a factorized formulation combining continuous specimen-domain coefficient fields with learned detector-domain basis patterns. Both are tested on recrystallized and additively manufactured Inconel 718.
AI.result: The factorized formulation achieves map-averaged reconstruction errors below 1% of maximum intensity, enables full-pattern super-resolution in specimen frame, continuous off-grid querying, spatially continuous boundary and heterogeneity localization via analytical derivatives, and 700-fold compression vs. raw pattern storage.
AI.conclusion: Neural EBSD successfully transforms discrete EBSD data into a continuous, differentiable representation that preserves high accuracy while enabling new capabilities (super-resolution, continuous querying, spatial derivatives) and massive compression.

title: Interplay between photon condensation and electron-electron interactions in molecular systems
summary: We investigate a minimal molecular model consisting of square planar plaquettes hosting multiple electrons, whose dynamics is governed by a tight-binding Hamiltonian supplemented by on-site Hubbard repulsion. By coupling this system to a spatially nonuniform cavity mode, we analyze the emergence of a magnetostatic instability, namely photon condensation, originating from the paramagnetic Van Vleck mechanism. The global behavior of the system is analyzed for different electronic filling factors, and we find that, except for the special cases of half-filling and single electron, where the transition, if it occurs, is necessarily a second order phase transition, the global system may also undergo a first order transition because of the action of the electron-electron interaction. The polaritonic excitation energies are analyzed, providing clear spectroscopic signatures of the magnetostatic instability and of its order.

AI.tldr: A theoretical study of photon condensation (magnetostatic instability) in a molecular model of square plaquettes coupled to a nonuniform cavity mode, showing that electron-electron interactions can drive either first- or second-order phase transitions depending on electronic filling.
AI.motivation: To understand the emergence of magnetostatic instabilities (photon condensation) via the paramagnetic Van Vleck mechanism in a minimal molecular system coupled to a spatially nonuniform cavity mode, and to characterize the order of the phase transition under different electronic filling conditions.
AI.method: A minimal molecular model of square planar plaquettes with multiple electrons, described by a tight-binding Hamiltonian plus on-site Hubbard repulsion, coupled to a spatially nonuniform cavity mode. The analysis explores different electronic filling factors and examines polaritonic excitation energies.
AI.result: Except at half-filling and single-electron cases (where the transition is necessarily second-order), the system can undergo a first-order phase transition due to electron-electron interactions. Clear spectroscopic signatures in the polaritonic excitation energies distinguish the instability and its order.
AI.conclusion: Electron-electron interactions can qualitatively change the nature of photon condensation transitions in cavity-coupled molecular systems, with the order of the transition tunable by the electronic filling factor.

title: Probing Spin Configurations in Exchange-Coupled Magnetic Bilayers with Orthogonal Anisotropies via Anomalous Hall and Nernst Effects
summary: When two ferromagnetic thin films with different magnetic easy axes are coupled via the exchange interaction, the magnetization process becomes nontrivial. In this paper, we demonstrate that three-dimensional magnetization information in such a bilayer system can be accessed electrically by combining measurements of the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and anomalous Nernst effect (ANE). Specifically, we investigate a CoFe$_2$O$_4$(001)/Fe bilayer, where the insulating nature of CoFe$_2$O$_4$ ensures that these transport measurements selectively probe only the conductive Fe layer. By combining the AHE and ANE results and comparing them with a simple micromagnetic simulation, we probe the magnetic configuration of antiferromagnetically coupled Fe layer and suggest the emergence of a twisted magnetic structure near the interface.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that combining anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) measurements enables electrical access to 3D magnetization information in exchange-coupled ferromagnetic bilayers. Studying a CoFe₂O₄(001)/Fe bilayer, the authors probe antiferromagnetically coupled Fe layer and suggest a twisted magnetic structure near the interface.
AI.motivation: To develop an electrical method for extracting three-dimensional magnetization information in exchange-coupled ferromagnetic bilayers with different easy axes, where the magnetization process is nontrivial.
AI.method: Combined measurements of anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) on a CoFe₂O₄(001)/Fe bilayer; results compared with micromagnetic simulations.
AI.result: The combination of AHE and ANE measurements, together with micromagnetic simulations, reveals the magnetic configuration of the antiferromagnetically coupled Fe layer and suggests a twisted magnetic structure near the interface.
AI.conclusion: Three-dimensional magnetization information in exchange-coupled bilayer systems can be accessed electrically by combining AHE and ANE measurements, enabling detection of nontrivial magnetic configurations such as twisted interfacial structures.

title: Quantum statistics in an extended collider coupled to a qubit
comment: Main text: 6 pages and 2 figures, Appendix: 13 pages
summary: Mesoscopic colliders provide an effective platform for probing the mutual statistics of quantum particles. Recent experiments have successfully extracted the mutual statistics of fermions, and more exotic anyons using quantum point contacts (QPCs). Coupling a point-like collider, such as a quantum point contact, to a two-level impurity or qubit can induce statistical transmutation of fermions, causing them to display boson-like bunching tendencies. Here, we extend the analysis to an extended collider. We investigate the scattering of two incoming fermionic and bosonic wave packets in the presence of post-selection on the impurity state, and systematically analyze the possible benchmarks used to characterize bunching and infer the underlying mutual statistics. We show that only a specific benchmark faithfully captures the mutual statistics of the colliding particles, while alternative choices can produce spurious statistical signatures. Hence, the correct benchmark for probing the quantum statistics depends on the intricate details of the mesoscopic collider.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates scattering of fermionic and bosonic wave packets in an extended collider coupled to a two-level impurity, showing that only a specific benchmark correctly captures mutual quantum statistics, while others can produce spurious statistical signatures.
AI.motivation: Mesoscopic colliders coupled to quantum impurities can induce statistical transmutation (e.g., fermions behaving like bosons). The authors aim to extend this analysis from point-like to extended colliders and systematically evaluate which benchmarks faithfully reflect underlying mutual statistics.
AI.method: The authors investigate scattering of two incoming fermionic and bosonic wave packets in the presence of post-selection on the impurity state, and systematically analyze various benchmarks used to characterize bunching and infer mutual statistics.
AI.result: Only a specific benchmark faithfully captures the mutual statistics of colliding particles; alternative choices can produce spurious statistical signatures. The correct benchmark depends on the intricate details of the mesoscopic collider.
AI.conclusion: The choice of benchmark for probing quantum statistics in mesoscopic colliders is non-trivial and must be carefully matched to the collider's details to avoid misinterpretation of statistical signatures.

title: Propagation and localization of spin excitations at altermagnetic domain walls
summary: Altermagnets (A$\ell$Ms) are spin-compensated materials in which opposite-spin sublattices are connected by a symmetry that causes a spin splitting in their elementary excitations. As there is a strong effect of altermagnetism on domain wall properties, it is quite natural to also expect an enrichment of the physics of magnetic excitations at A$\ell$M domain walls. Here, we consider the propagation of spin eigen-excitations along domain walls in easy-axial $d$-wave A$\ell$Ms. Investigating the presence of bound states localized on a domain wall, we find that the effect of the A$\ell$M on the bound states strongly depends on the orientation of the domain wall relative to the crystallographic directions. If the domain wall is oriented along a nodal direction [100] or [010], A$\ell$M does not change the number of bound states; however, it leads to a nonlinear dispersion and a tilt of the wavefront. The effect of A$\ell$M is strongest when the domain wall is oriented along the directions [110] or [$\bar{1}$10], i.e., along the directions of the strongest A$\ell$M splitting in the magnon spectrum. In this case, (i) the additional gapped bound states appear, (ii) degeneracy of the eigenstates with respect to their polarization (right-handed or left-handed precession of the N{é}el vector) is removed, and (iii) the localization area of the bound states strongly depends on the eigenfrequency. The latter may lead to strong localization of the bound state at the domain wall. We further consider the influence of a static magnetic field that is applied along the easy axis, and find that the magnetic field induces an asymmetry between the localization regions on opposite sides of the domain wall and sets an upper limit on the absolute value of the propagating eigenstate's wave vector.

AI.tldr: This paper studies spin eigen-excitations (bound states) propagating along domain walls in easy-axial d-wave altermagnets, finding that their properties—such as number, dispersion, polarization degeneracy, and localization—depend strongly on domain wall orientation relative to crystallographic axes, with the strongest altermagnet effects occurring along [110]/[1̄10] directions, and that an applied magnetic field breaks asymmetry and limits wave vector magnitude.
AI.motivation: Since altermagnetism strongly affects domain wall properties, it is natural to expect an enrichment of magnetic excitation physics at altermagnet domain walls, motivating the investigation of bound states localized on such walls.
AI.method: The authors theoretically analyze spin eigen-excitations propagating along domain walls in easy-axial d-wave altermagnets, considering different domain wall orientations ([100], [010], [110], [1̄10]) and the influence of an external static magnetic field applied along the easy axis.
AI.result: (1) For domain walls along [100]/[010] (nodal directions), altermagnetism does not change the number of bound states but induces nonlinear dispersion and wavefront tilt. (2) For domain walls along [110]/[1̄10] (strongest splitting directions), additional gapped bound states appear, polarization degeneracy is lifted, and localization depends strongly on eigenfrequency. (3) A static magnetic field breaks symmetry between localization regions on opposite sides and sets an upper limit on the wave vector of propagating eigenstates.
AI.conclusion: Altermagnetism enriches the physics of magnetic excitations at domain walls in an orientation-dependent manner, with the strongest effects along [110]/[1̄10] directions, and external magnetic fields can further tune these bound states.

title: Optical-like interference control polar-phonons dispersions in 2D materials
summary: It has been argued that the polar phonon modes of two-dimensional (2D) materials should show a linear dependence close to the Brillouin zone center due to the reduced problem dimensionality compared to a three-dimensional crystal, leading to a vanishing LO-TO splitting. Revisiting this question using a mirror-charge framework derived from classical electrostatics, we show that it is not always true: with perfectly-reflective dielectric interfaces, it is possible to recover a LO-TO splitting, or an equivalent phenomenon for the out-of-plane modes. Effectively, the dispersion of polar phonon modes is governed by optical-like constructive and destructive interferences of the source potential with its reflection at the dielectric interfaces. This work highlights the critical role of dielectric boundary conditions to understand phonon-related properties in 2D materials.

AI.tldr: Contrary to prior belief, LO-TO splitting can exist in 2D polar phonon modes under perfectly-reflective dielectric interfaces, governed by optical-like interference of source potentials with their reflections.
AI.motivation: To revisit the prevailing assumption that polar phonon modes in 2D materials show linear dispersion near the Brillouin zone center with vanishing LO-TO splitting due to reduced dimensionality.
AI.method: A mirror-charge framework derived from classical electrostatics is used to analyze the dielectric boundary conditions and their effect on polar phonon dispersion in 2D materials.
AI.result: LO-TO splitting can be recovered in 2D materials when perfectly-reflective dielectric interfaces are present, with dispersion governed by constructive/destructive interference between the source potential and its reflections.
AI.conclusion: Dielectric boundary conditions play a critical role in determining phonon-related properties in 2D materials, challenging the notion that LO-TO splitting universally vanishes in reduced dimensions.

title: Nonequilibrium Green Functions Simulations for Large Correlated Systems
summary: Correlated real-time dynamics in large, spatially inhomogeneous quantum systems remain difficult to access with nonequilibrium many-body methods. Two-time nonequilibrium Green functions (NEGF) retain dynamical correlations but their computational runtime grows cubically with the number of time steps $N_\mathrm{t}$. This scaling bottleneck could recently be overcome by introducing the G1--G2 scheme that is linear in $N_\mathrm{t}$, but requires propagation of a two-particle correlation function and may suffer from numerical instabilities. This has restricted simulations to small systems with $N_\mathrm{b} \sim 10^2$ basis states. Here we introduce a quantum-fluctuation formulation of nonequilibrium Green functions, denoted $δ$NEGF, that represents dynamical two-particle correlations through fluctuations of field-operator products, $δ\hat G$. This guarantees stable dynamics by preserving the positivity of the reduced density matrices, avoids the explicit storage of the two-particle Green function, and reduces the propagation to a finite ensemble of Hartree-Fock-like trajectories. Combined with a stochastic low-rank decomposition of the correlation functions, the method retains time-linear scaling while extending dynamical $GW$ and particle-particle and particle-hole $T$-matrix simulations to basis sizes of order $N_\mathrm{b}\sim 10^4$. We benchmark $δ$NEGF against exact and HF-GKBA results for lattice systems, finding stable correlated dynamics also at strong coupling. We further demonstrate large-scale simulations of diffusion in two-dimensional Hubbard lattices and ultrafast relaxation in graphene nanoribbon heterostructures with long-range Coulomb interactions. These results establish $δ$NEGF as a scalable route to dynamical self-energy simulations of large, spatially inhomogeneous correlated quantum systems beyond the reach of existing NEGF implementations.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces δNEGF, a quantum-fluctuation formulation of nonequilibrium Green functions that replaces the two-particle Green function with stochastic fluctuations of field-operator products. This method achieves linear scaling in time steps (like G1-G2) but with improved numerical stability and reduced memory requirements, enabling simulations of spatially inhomogeneous quantum systems with up to ~10^4 basis states—two orders of magnitude larger than previous NEGF approaches.
AI.motivation: Existing NEGF methods face a computational bottleneck: traditional two-time NEGF scales cubically with time steps (N_t^3), while the recent G1-G2 scheme achieves linear scaling but suffers from numerical instabilities and requires explicit storage of the computationally expensive two-particle correlation function, limiting simulations to small systems with N_b ~ 10^2 basis states.
AI.method: The δNEGF method represents dynamical two-particle correlations through fluctuations of field-operator products (δĜ), preserving positivity of reduced density matrices for stable dynamics. It avoids explicit storage of the two-particle Green function and reduces propagation to a finite ensemble of Hartree-Fock-like trajectories. Combined with stochastic low-rank decomposition of correlation functions, it retains time-linear scaling.
AI.result: δNEGF extends dynamical GW and particle-particle/particle-hole T-matrix simulations to basis sizes up to N_b ~ 10^4. Benchmarks against exact and HF-GKBA results for lattice systems show stable correlated dynamics even at strong coupling. Large-scale demonstrations include diffusion in 2D Hubbard lattices and ultrafast relaxation in graphene nanoribbon heterostructures with long-range Coulomb interactions.
AI.conclusion: δNEGF establishes a scalable route to dynamical self-energy simulations for large, spatially inhomogeneous correlated quantum systems that are beyond the reach of existing NEGF implementations.

title: Extending Field Limits in Nanoscale Magnetic Imaging with Metamaterial-inspired Magnetic Flux Concentrators
comment: Submitted and accepted manuscript versions for Small (Wiley). To be published (Article DOI: 10.1002/smll.202600073)
summary: Many nanoscale magnetic imaging techniques are constrained by the maximum magnetic field that can be applied during measurements, due to geometrical limitations or interactions with the probe or the detected signal (e.g., electrons). Here, it is demonstrated that sample-integrated metamaterial-inspired magnetic flux concentrators (MFCs) locally amplify magnetic fields, allowing observation of magnetization processes beyond instrumental limits. Micrometer-sized MFCs fabricated directly on the samples are tested in photoemission electron microscopy experiments employing X-ray magnetic circular dichroism as magnetic contrast mechanism. At low applied fields, substantial amplification factors enable observation of magnetization reversal in a chain of magnetite nanoparticles synthesized by magnetotactic bacteria at an applied field of 8 mT, substantially smaller than the 50 mT predicted by simulations in absence of MFCs. At higher fields, the field enhancement extends the accessible field range by a factor of five, enabling for the first time, imaging of the field-dependent magnetic domain structure evolution of an isolated giant magnetofossil. Finally, we show how MFC geometry and material parameters can be tuned to optimize performance considering sample and experimental constraints, providing a tunable and broadly applicable strategy for extending the accessible field range in a wide variety of nanoscale magnetic imaging techniques.

AI.tldr: Sample-integrated metamaterial-inspired magnetic flux concentrators (MFCs) locally amplify magnetic fields, enabling nanoscale magnetic imaging beyond instrumental limits. Demonstrated in photoemission electron microscopy with XMCD, MFCs allowed observation of magnetization reversal in magnetite nanoparticles at 8 mT (vs. 50 mT predicted) and extended the accessible field range fivefold for imaging domain structures in giant magnetofossils.
AI.motivation: Many nanoscale magnetic imaging techniques are constrained by the maximum magnetic field achievable during measurements due to geometrical limitations or probe/signal interactions, limiting observation of magnetization processes.
AI.method: Sample-integrated metamaterial-inspired magnetic flux concentrators (MFCs) were fabricated directly on samples and tested in photoemission electron microscopy experiments using X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) for magnetic contrast.
AI.result: At low fields, MFCs enabled observation of magnetization reversal in magnetite nanoparticles at 8 mT, far below the 50 mT predicted without MFCs. At higher fields, the accessible field range was extended fivefold, enabling first-time imaging of field-dependent domain structure evolution in an isolated giant magnetofossil. MFC geometry and material parameters can be tuned to optimize performance.
AI.conclusion: MFCs provide a tunable, broadly applicable strategy for extending the accessible field range across a wide variety of nanoscale magnetic imaging techniques.

title: Fractional shot noise of an SU(N) Kondo system
summary: We consider transport through a multi-level interacting quantum dot (N-QD) in Kondo regime. Using the Kotliar-Ruckentein slave boson approach (SBMFA) for N-level Anderson model we define effectively noninteracting quasiparticles of the SU(N) Kondo system ($N=2,3,4,5,6$). Kondo resonance transmission coefficients determine linear noise describing quasiparticle partitioning. To discuss nonlinear conductance, susceptibilities and shot noise in the strong coupling regime, we apply Fermi liquid theory with parameters expressed by susceptibilities of pseudofermions determined within SBMFA. Nonlinear shot noise is dominated by two-quasiparticle scattering. However, we demonstrate that for occupation regions distant from the electron-hole symmetry point, the role of three-body correlations must be revealed.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes transport through multi-level interacting quantum dots in the Kondo regime using slave boson and Fermi liquid approaches, finding that nonlinear shot noise is dominated by two-quasiparticle scattering but three-body correlations become important away from electron-hole symmetry.
AI.motivation: To understand transport properties, noise, and correlation effects in multi-level quantum dots operating in the Kondo regime, particularly beyond the electron-hole symmetry point.
AI.method: Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave boson mean-field approach (SBMFA) for N-level Anderson model (N=2-6) combined with Fermi liquid theory using pseudofermion susceptibilities.
AI.result: Two-quasiparticle scattering dominates nonlinear shot noise, but three-body correlations become significant for occupation regions away from electron-hole symmetry.
AI.conclusion: Three-body correlations must be accounted for when analyzing nonlinear shot noise in multi-level quantum dots in the Kondo regime away from electron-hole symmetry.

title: Ultra-Soft Ferrimagnetism in a High-Entropy Spinel Oxide Driven by Site-Selective Cation Disorder
summary: High-entropy materials are complex, multifunctional materials that have reshaped the design of advanced functional materials. Their chemically diverse compositions enable access to a broader compositional space than conventional solid solutions, while simultaneously posing significant challenges for fundamental structure property understanding. In this study, we introduce a new highentropy spinel oxide with an exceptionally low coercivity of 1.8 Oe at room temperature, among the lowest reported for bulk spinel oxides, and a high electrical resistivity (1560 ohm-cm). Neutron powder diffraction (NPD) and magnetic measurements reveal long-range collinear ferrimagnetic ordering (k = 0,0,0) with a transition temperature at 420 K. This rare combination of ultra-soft magnetic behavior, robust ferrimagnetic ordering well above room temperature, and high resistivity highlights its strong potential as an advanced soft-magnetic oxide for low-loss, high-frequency applications. Furthermore, X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), Mossbauer spectroscopy, and NPD analyses were combined to determine the cation distribution and site selectivity across the tetrahedral and octahedral sites of the complex structure.

AI.tldr: A new high-entropy spinel oxide with ultra-low coercivity (1.8 Oe), high resistivity (1560 Ω·cm), and robust ferrimagnetic ordering above room temperature (Tc ~420 K) is reported, showing potential for low-loss, high-frequency soft magnetic applications.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of fundamental structure-property understanding in high-entropy materials and to develop a new soft magnetic oxide with low coercivity, high resistivity, and robust magnetic ordering for high-frequency applications.
AI.method: Combined neutron powder diffraction (NPD), X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), Mössbauer spectroscopy, and magnetic measurements to characterize crystal structure, cation distribution, and magnetic ordering.
AI.result: Achieved exceptional combination of ultra-soft magnetism (coercivity ~1.8 Oe), high electrical resistivity (~1560 Ω·cm), and long-range collinear ferrimagnetic ordering (k = 0,0,0) with Tc ~420 K in a high-entropy spinel oxide.
AI.conclusion: The high-entropy spinel oxide is a promising advanced soft-magnetic material for low-loss, high-frequency applications, demonstrating that complex compositional space can yield rare property combinations.

title: Thermal Signatures of the Slater-Mott Crossover in the Hubbard Model: From Double Occupancy to Antiferromagnetic Correlation Length
summary: The interaction-driven crossover from a Slater insulator to a Mott insulator in the Néel-ordered ground state of the Hubbard model is a fundamental paradigm of strongly correlated electrons, yet its quantitative characterization has remained elusive. Here we establish a clear and experimentally accessible thermal criterion for this crossover via the sign change of the temperature derivative of double occupancy, $(\partial D/\partial T)_U$, near zero temperature. In the Slater regime, $(\partial D/\partial T)_U>0$ reflects the major role of charge fluctuations; in the Mott regime, the anomalous $(\partial D/\partial T)_U<0$, a manifestation of the Pomeranchuk effect, signals the dominance of low-energy spin superexchange physics. Using exact diagonalization and {\it numerically exact} quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this criterion determines the crossover boundary at $U_{\rm cross}/t=4.0(2)$ for the half-filled two-dimensional Hubbard model. Furthermore, we obtain a consistent boundary independently from the maximum in the antiferromagnetic correlation length, which also arises from the superexchange physics. These two thermal signatures are theoretically unified through the local minimum of thermal entropy versus interaction $U$ at low temperatures. Our results offer a direct, measurable, and physically intuitive framework to identify the Slater-Mott crossover in optical lattice experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a thermal criterion to distinguish Slater vs. Mott insulating behavior in the Hubbard model via the sign of (∂D/∂T)_U, identifies the crossover at U_cross/t=4.0(2) for the 2D Hubbard model, and links it to antiferromagnetic correlation length and entropy minima.
AI.motivation: The Slater-to-Mott insulator crossover in the Hubbard model is a fundamental strongly correlated electron paradigm, but its quantitative characterization has remained elusive.
AI.method: Using exact diagonalization and numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, the crossover is identified via the sign change of (∂D/∂T)_U near zero temperature, and independently via the maximum in antiferromagnetic correlation length.
AI.result: The crossover boundary is at U_cross/t=4.0(2) for the half-filled 2D Hubbard model; the two thermal signatures are unified through the local minimum of entropy vs. interaction U at low temperatures.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a direct, measurable, and physically intuitive framework to identify the Slater-Mott crossover in optical lattice experiments.

title: Layer-parity-dependent interfacial coupling in Nb$_3$Cl$_8$/graphene van der Waals heterostructures
summary: Strongly correlated two-dimensional systems provide compelling platforms for investigating exotic quantum phenomena. Niobium chloride (Nb$_3$Cl$_8$), a single-band Mott insulator, exhibits a remarkable out-of-plane polarization in its topmost layer that oscillates with layer parity, manifesting as an odd-even effect. Using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM), this layer-parity-dependent polarization can be effectively characterized through surface morphology and potential mapping, enabling the unambiguous identification of different surface phases. We then fabricated dual-gate Hall devices by coupling different surface phases of Nb$_3$Cl$_8$ with monolayer graphene to investigate how the topmost-layer out-of-plane polarization influences interfacial coupling and the resulting transport behavior. Our results reveal significant phase-dependent variations in charge transfer, carrier densities, and hybridization gaps (25.2 meV for Phase 1 and 30.0 meV for Phase 2). Density functional theory calculations corroborate these experimental findings, showing that distinct out-of-plane polarizations in the topmost layer lead to different orbital overlaps and interfacial coupling strengths. These findings highlight the critical importance of surface polarization and orbital orientation in engineering the properties of strongly correlated van der Waals heterostructures.

AI.tldr: Nb₃Cl₈ exhibits a layer-parity-dependent out-of-plane polarization in its topmost layer, which can be characterized via AFM/KPFM and used to modulate interfacial coupling and transport when combined with graphene, showing phase-dependent charge transfer and hybridization gaps (25.2–30.0 meV).
AI.motivation: To investigate how the topmost-layer out-of-plane polarization in a strongly correlated 2D Mott insulator (Nb₃Cl₈) influences interfacial coupling and transport behavior in van der Waals heterostructures.
AI.method: AFM and KPFM for surface characterization; dual-gate Hall devices coupling Nb₃Cl₈ surface phases with monolayer graphene; DFT calculations for theoretical validation.
AI.result: Significant phase-dependent variations in charge transfer, carrier densities, and hybridization gaps (25.2 meV for Phase 1, 30.0 meV for Phase 2); DFT confirms distinct out-of-plane polarizations lead to different orbital overlaps and interfacial coupling strengths.
AI.conclusion: Surface polarization and orbital orientation are critical for engineering properties of strongly correlated van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Flower-like WO3-modified Vulcan carbon GDEs for photoelectro-Fenton process: Efficient ciprofloxacin degradation and mechanistic insights
summary: Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis was investigated using a 3 percent WO3 C gas diffusion electrode GDE. The catalyst outperformed bare Vulcan carbon, generating H2O2 concentrations of 423, 586, and 916 mg L at 50, 75, and 100 mA cm2, respectively, maintaining around 70 percent current efficiency. This performance and lower energy consumption are attributed to the WO3 carbon synergistic effect. In electro Fenton EF applications, the WO3 C GDE achieved rapid initial ciprofloxacin CIP degradation of around 70 percent in 30 min, though limited later by slow Fe2 regeneration. Incorporating UV light photoelectro Fenton overcame this constraint, yielding complete CIP removal within 90 min, while a boron doped diamond BDD anode enhanced total organic carbon TOC mineralization to 66 percent. The proposed degradation mechanism proceeds via hydroxyl radical attack on the piperazine ring with or without defluorination and quinolone ring oxidation, with theoretical analysis confirming reduced environmental toxicity of the transformation products. Overall, WO3 C GDEs represent a highly efficient strategy for H2O2 generation and wastewater remediation.

AI.tldr: WO3/C gas diffusion electrode efficiently generates H2O2 (up to 916 mg/L at 100 mA cm²) for wastewater treatment. Combined with photoelectro-Fenton and BDD anode, it achieves complete ciprofloxacin degradation in 90 min with 66% TOC mineralization via hydroxyl radical attack on piperazine ring.
AI.motivation: To develop an efficient electrocatalyst for H2O2 synthesis and improve wastewater remediation, addressing limitations of conventional electro-Fenton processes (slow Fe²⁺ regeneration) for antibiotic degradation.
AI.method: 3% WO3/C gas diffusion electrode (GDE) for H2O2 electrosynthesis; electro-Fenton (EF) and photoelectro-Fenton (PEF) with UV light; boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode; theoretical analysis of degradation pathway and toxicity.
AI.result: WO3/C GDE produced 423, 586, 916 mg/L H2O2 at 50, 75, 100 mA/cm² (~70% current efficiency). EF achieved ~70% CIP degradation in 30 min; PEF achieved complete removal in 90 min; BDD anode yielded 66% TOC mineralization.
AI.conclusion: WO3/C GDE is a highly efficient strategy for H2O2 generation and wastewater remediation, with synergistic effects enhancing performance and reducing energy consumption.

title: Field-Induced Up-Up-Down State and Frustrated Magnetism in a Non-Kramers Triangular Antiferromagnet
summary: A previously unreported triangular lattice (TL) antiferromagnet, TmZnGaO4, was synthesized as single crystals, and its crystal structure, magnetic susceptibilities, and specific heat were reported. Its crystal structure is isomorphic to that of the transverse-field Ising antiferromagnet TmMgGaO4, with Tm3+ ions located in the TLs, separated by a nonmagnetic bilayer composed mainly of Ga3+ and Zn2+ ions. The magnetic susceptibilities indicate the dominating antiferromagnetic interactions. The magnetization curves (M-H) exhibit strong easy-c-axis anisotropy, with a clear one-third magnetic plateau emerging, consistent with a field-induced up-up-down spin configuration. Instead of forming a conventional long-range magnetic order, the system exhibits two broad anomalies at 0.11 K and 2.81 K in zero-field specific heat measurements, highlighting the persistence of strong spin fluctuations and the potential for exotic quantum spin states. The above results reveal its future interest in exploring exotic quantum spin states in TmZnGaO4.

AI.tldr: TmZnGaO4 is a newly synthesized triangular lattice antiferromagnet exhibiting strong easy-c-axis anisotropy, a one-third magnetization plateau, and two broad specific heat anomalies at low temperatures (0.11 K and 2.81 K), suggesting the absence of conventional long-range order and the presence of exotic quantum spin states.
AI.motivation: To report the synthesis and characterization of a previously unreported triangular lattice antiferromagnet, TmZnGaO4, and investigate its potential for hosting exotic quantum spin states due to strong spin fluctuations and the absence of conventional long-range magnetic order.
AI.method: Single crystals of TmZnGaO4 were synthesized, and its crystal structure, magnetic susceptibilities, magnetization curves (M-H), and specific heat were measured and analyzed.
AI.result: (1) Crystal structure is isomorphic to TmMgGaO4 with Tm3+ ions on triangular lattices separated by nonmagnetic Ga3+/Zn2+ bilayers; (2) Magnetic susceptibilities show dominant antiferromagnetic interactions; (3) M-H curves exhibit strong easy-c-axis anisotropy with a clear one-third magnetization plateau (field-induced up-up-down spin configuration); (4) Zero-field specific heat shows two broad anomalies at 0.11 K and 2.81 K, indicating strong spin fluctuations without conventional long-range order.
AI.conclusion: TmZnGaO4 is a promising candidate for exploring exotic quantum spin states due to its triangular lattice geometry, absence of conventional magnetic ordering, and persistent spin fluctuations at low temperatures.

title: Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in $PT$ antiferromagnets
summary: Surface altermagnetism extends spin splitting beyond bulk altermagnets through symmetry reduction at surfaces and interfaces. An existing classification applies to the local symmetry of atomically flat surface terraces. The present paper addresses the symmetry of macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces. These correlations are governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue point group. Rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden at any surface of a magnet whose antisymmetry space group contains antitranslations, and the classification therefore reduces to $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets. By restoring all symmetries leaving the surface normal invariant, roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations, increase the surface symmetry, or suppress spin splitting. By combining bulk switchability with altermagnetic surface transport properties, roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets provides a route toward spintronic functionality.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the classification of surface altermagnetism to rough surfaces, showing that roughness-robust surface altermagnetism is governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue group, exists only in PT-symmetric antiferromagnets, and can generate, enhance, or suppress spin splitting depending on symmetry restoration.
AI.motivation: Existing classification of surface altermagnetism only applies to atomically flat surface terraces; this paper addresses the gap by analyzing macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces.
AI.method: The authors use the concept of the surface antisymmetry Laue point group to determine which spin-momentum correlations survive averaging over rough surfaces, and classify allowed rough-surface altermagnetism based on the antisymmetry space group of the bulk magnet.
AI.result: Rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden in magnets whose antisymmetry space group contains antitranslations, reducing the classification to PT-symmetric antiferromagnets. Roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations, increase surface symmetry, or suppress spin splitting.
AI.conclusion: Combining bulk switchability with altermagnetic surface transport properties in PT-symmetric antiferromagnets offers a practical route toward spintronic device functionality that is robust against surface roughness.

title: Hybrid Hamiltonian-diagrammatic quantum impurity solver
summary: Quantum impurity models, which describe the coupling between interacting orbitals and a non-interacting bath, play a central role in the physics of strongly correlated electron systems. Solving a quantum impurity model in general requires the use of non-perturbative numerical methods. Hamiltonian-based approaches, which rely on an explicit bath discretization, are typically limited to a small number of bath sites or small entanglement, and diagrammatic methods suffer from sign problems, slow convergence, or diagram truncation approximations. Here we show that these two classes of methods can be combined: augmenting diagrammatic methods with a small auxiliary bath can reduce the residual problem to a regime where low-order perturbation theory is highly accurate and rapidly converging. In a simple benchmark, the precision of the hybrid approach surpasses bold-line calculations by several orders of magnitude; for a strongly interacting two-orbital model with a severe sign problem, convergence is achieved at three orders of magnitude lower computational cost than competing methods; and convergence to the unknown exact result is rapidly accelerated in a difficult realistic problem. Our results establish a practical route to high-precision quantum impurity solutions in correlated quantum systems.

AI.tldr: A hybrid approach combining Hamiltonian-based bath discretization with diagrammatic methods solves quantum impurity models with dramatically improved precision, lower computational cost, and faster convergence than either method alone.
AI.motivation: Quantum impurity models are central to strongly correlated electron systems but existing methods have limitations: Hamiltonian-based approaches are limited to small bath sites or low entanglement, while diagrammatic methods suffer from sign problems, slow convergence, or truncation approximations. The authors aim to overcome these limitations.
AI.method: The hybrid approach augments diagrammatic methods with a small auxiliary bath, reducing the residual problem to a regime where low-order perturbation theory becomes highly accurate and rapidly converging.
AI.result: (1) On a simple benchmark, hybrid precision surpasses bold-line calculations by several orders of magnitude. (2) For a strongly interacting two-orbital model with a severe sign problem, convergence is achieved at three orders of magnitude lower computational cost. (3) Convergence to the unknown exact result is rapidly accelerated in a difficult realistic problem.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid approach establishes a practical route to high-precision quantum impurity solutions in correlated quantum systems.

title: Degeneracy and trajectory control of spin eigenmodes excited by fs-optical pulses in a nearly compensated ferrimagnet
summary: We investigate optically excited spin dynamics in a uniaxial ferrimagnet near the magnetization compensation point under a magnetic field applied along the magnetic anisotropy axis. Experiment and numerical modeling reveal an unusual regime where the frequencies of two spin eigenmodes approach each other and become highly field sensitive. The modes, corresponding to opposite rotations of the Neel vector, simultaneously reverse their handedness at a critical field where their frequencies become degenerate. At this point, the two-frequency precessional dynamics collapses into a linear oscillations directed along the inverse-Faraday-effect excitation induced by a single pump pulse. We further show that a double-pulse excitation scheme enables control of the spin trajectory. These results uncover an unconventional dynamical regime in ferrimagnets and establish new opportunities for manipulating spin motion in magnonic systems and devices.

AI.tldr: Optically excited spin dynamics in a uniaxial ferrimagnet near the magnetization compensation point reveals a regime where two spin eigenmodes become degenerate and reverse handedness at a critical field, collapsing into linear oscillations; double-pulse excitation enables spin trajectory control.
AI.motivation: To investigate the unusual dynamical regime of spin eigenmodes in ferrimagnets near the magnetization compensation point under an applied magnetic field, where mode frequencies approach each other and become highly field-sensitive.
AI.method: Combined experimental and numerical modeling approach, using optical excitation (single and double pump pulses) to study spin dynamics in a uniaxial ferrimagnet with field applied along the magnetic anisotropy axis.
AI.result: Two spin eigenmodes (corresponding to opposite rotations of the Néel vector) become degenerate at a critical field and simultaneously reverse their handedness; the precessional dynamics collapses into linear oscillations along the inverse-Faraday-effect excitation direction.
AI.conclusion: This work uncovers an unconventional dynamical regime in ferrimagnets and establishes new opportunities for manipulating spin motion in magnonic systems and devices via double-pulse excitation schemes.

title: Ab initio study of magnetism in pristine and defective MnBi2Te4
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Includes Appendix and Supplemental Material
summary: The magnetic material MnBi2Te4 (MBT) has garnered significant attention due to its unique combination of long-range antiferromagnetism and nontrivial topological electronic properties. However, experimental measurements report inconsistent magnetizations, which could be attributed to a variety of intrinsic defects. To date, a comprehensive investigation of defect-engineered MBT systems has not yet been established. Employing state-of-the-art $ab~initio$ techniques, this work systematically investigates the influence of various experimentally reported defects on the magnetic properties of bulk and monolayer MBT at different concentrations. Mn-vacancy and Mn-rich defects are found to enhance the ferromagnetism of bulk MBT. The investigation of Mn-rich and intermixing defects in the monolayer reveals that subtle structural and electronic modifications can alter the magnetic coupling. Projection onto a Heisenberg Hamiltonian demonstrates that defects modify exchange interactions, thereby giving rise to distinct magnetic ground states. This work sheds light on magnetic coupling mechanisms and provides guidelines for the experimental control of magnetism in MnBi2Te4.

AI.tldr: This paper uses ab initio techniques to systematically study how various intrinsic defects (Mn-vacancy, Mn-rich, intermixing) affect the magnetic properties of bulk and monolayer MnBi₂Te₄, showing that defects modify exchange interactions and can alter magnetic ground states, with Mn-vacancy and Mn-rich defects enhancing ferromagnetism in bulk.
AI.motivation: Experimental measurements report inconsistent magnetizations in MnBi₂Te₄, potentially due to intrinsic defects, yet a comprehensive investigation of defect-engineered MBT systems has not been established.
AI.method: State-of-the-art ab initio techniques (DFT) combined with projection onto a Heisenberg Hamiltonian to systematically investigate various experimentally reported defects at different concentrations in bulk and monolayer MBT.
AI.result: Mn-vacancy and Mn-rich defects enhance ferromagnetism in bulk MBT. In monolayers, Mn-rich and intermixing defects cause subtle structural/electronic modifications that alter magnetic coupling. Defects modify exchange interactions, giving rise to distinct magnetic ground states.
AI.conclusion: This work clarifies magnetic coupling mechanisms in defective MnBi₂Te₄ and provides guidelines for experimental control of magnetism in this material.

title: Direction-Dependent Quantum Transport Properties of MoS$_2$ Integrated into Biphenylene Configuration
summary: Motivated by the experimental realization of the two-dimensional (2D) carbon biphenylene network (BPN), the theoretical extension of the BPN topology to various groups of elements was successfully implemented.
